Standardized measures of a random-effect fit

Source: R/standardize_mixed.R
standardize_mixed.Rd

Indirect or direct standardization of every provider's outcome from a random-effect model: ratios and rates for the logistic models, differences for the linear models.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'logistic_re'
standardize(
  fit,
  type = c("indirect", "direct"),
  numerator = c("observed", "predicted"),
  null = "median",
  n_pop = NULL,
  providers = NULL,
  alpha_se = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  threads = 1,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'linear_re'
standardize(
  fit,
  type = c("indirect", "direct"),
  numerator = c("observed", "predicted"),
  null = "median",
  providers = NULL,
  alpha_se = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

a model from fit_logistic_re(), fit_logistic_cre(), fit_linear_re() or fit_linear_cre().

type

"indirect" (default) or "direct".

numerator

for indirect standardization, the provider's "observed" outcome (default) or its "predicted" outcome under the fitted model with the provider's random effect, \(\sum_{j \in i} N_{ij}\, \hat p_{ij}\) (a shrunken numerator, as in predicted-to-expected ratios).

null

for indirect standardization, the norm of the random effect: "median" (default) or "mean" (weighted by rows) of the predicted effects, or a number (0 is the population intercept).

n_pop

denominator of the rates (logistic models); defaults to the number of trials among the fitted rows.

providers

optional subset of provider identifiers.

alpha_se

optional standard errors of the random effects, named by provider; with them the direct rate's standard error (logistic) or the difference's standard error (linear) is returned.

level

if given, confidence limits are added, mapped from Wald limits of \(\alpha_i\) (see confint.logistic_re()); for the logistic models only with numerator = "predicted", whose limits are the numerator evaluated at the limits of \(\alpha_i\).

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

threads

OpenMP threads for direct standardization.

...

unused.

Value

A data frame with one row per provider. Logistic models: provider, observed (the numerator), expected, ratio, rate, variance_expected and, when requested, se_rate, lower_ratio, upper_ratio, lower_rate, upper_rate. Linear models: provider, observed, expected, difference and, when requested, se_difference, lower, upper. Attributes type, numerator, null_value, level (and n_pop, population_rate for the logistic models).

Details

With \(\eta_{ij} = \hat\mu + Z_{ij}^\top\hat\beta\) the fixed part of the linear predictor and \(p_{ij}(a) = \mathrm{expit}(a + \eta_{ij})\):

  • logistic, indirect: \(E_i = \sum_{j \in i} N_{ij}\, p_{ij}(\alpha_0)\), ratio = numerator / \(E_i\);

  • logistic, direct: \(E_i = \sum_k N_k\, p_k(\hat\alpha_i)\) over every fitted row, ratio \(E_i / \sum O\);

  • linear, indirect: \(E_i = \sum_{j \in i} (\alpha_0 + \eta_{ij})\), difference = (numerator \(- E_i) / n_i\);

  • linear, direct: \(E_i = \sum_k (\hat\alpha_i + \eta_k)\), difference \((E_i - \sum O) / n\).

Rates are ratio \(\times \sum O / n_{pop}\), truncated to [0, 1].

Examples

# \donttest{
d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_logistic_re(pd)
head(standardize(fit, numerator = "predicted", level = 0.95))
